@graph.name: Insurance Claim Help
@graph.description: Get roof insurance claim help from R&C Roofing Contractors on Oahu. We inspect roof damage, document findings, provide roofing scope information, and complete approved repair work.

mainEntity.name: Should I call R&C before filing an insurance claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A professional inspection gives you the structural facts you need before deciding whether to file a claim with your carrier.

mainEntity.name: Can R&C tell me whether my roof damage is covered?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We identify the physical damage, but your insurance carrier determines coverage based entirely on the terms of your policy.

mainEntity.name: Does R&C negotiate with the insurance company?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We are not public adjusters. We provide contractor-side documentation and answer technical questions, but we do not negotiate settlements.

mainEntity.name: What if my insurance claim is denied?

acceptedAnswer.text: Review your carrier's explanation alongside your policy documents. If your carrier needs additional physical evidence, we can inspect the property again to document relevant conditions.

mainEntity.name: Can R&C complete the repair or replacement after the claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We operate under Hawaii Contractor License CT-33642 and can execute the agreed-upon repair or full replacement once your project moves forward.

@graph.name: Denied or Underpaid Claims
@graph.description: If your Hawaii roof claim was denied or the approved scope does not match the roofing work needed, R&C can inspect the roof and provide contractor-side documentation.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if my insurance claim was denied?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start by reviewing the carrier's written explanation. If you need clarity on the physical condition of the roof itself, R&C can inspect the property and provide objective contractor-side findings.

mainEntity.name: Can R&C overturn a denied insurance claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We do not make insurance coverage decisions and cannot legally force a carrier to change their ruling. We simply provide the physical roof documentation.

mainEntity.name: What does it mean if the insurance estimate is lower than the contractor estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually means the carrier and the contractor are using different scopes of work or project assumptions. We can explain what is required to fix your roof properly, but your carrier decides what costs they will cover.

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a public adjuster or an attorney?

acceptedAnswer.text: R&C cannot advise you on legal representation or public adjusting. If you need help interpreting your policy or fighting a disputed denial, you should speak with a licensed insurance professional.

mainEntity.name: Can R&C complete the repairs if the claim gets reopened?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We operate under Hawaii Contractor License CT-33642 and can execute the approved repair or full replacement once your project is cleared to move forward.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my roof has wind damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Visible signs include missing materials, new leaks, or debris impact. Wind uplift often breaks seals without blowing shingles off entirely, which requires a professional inspection to identify.

mainEntity.name: Should I climb onto my roof after a storm?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Wet or damaged roofs create severe safety risks.

mainEntity.name: Can R&C document storm damage for an insurance claim?

mainEntity.name: Does homeowners insurance cover roof wind damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coverage depends entirely on the terms and exclusions of your individual policy.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. You only need an inspection if you notice a new leak, displaced materials, or visible debris impact after severe weather.

mainEntity.name: What is the best roofing material for a home on Oahu?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single "best" material for every property. The right choice depends on your roof's design, neighborhood weather exposure, structural load capacity, and budget.

mainEntity.name: Does living near the ocean affect my roofing material choice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Coastal salt air can accelerate corrosion on certain exposed metal fasteners, flashing, and finishes, making material and component selection critical for oceanfront properties.

mainEntity.name: Can I change to a different roofing material during a replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, but it depends on your existing roof structure, roof pitch, and weight capacity. We evaluate these factors before recommending a material switch.

mainEntity.name: Should I choose my roofing material before scheduling an inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If you are unsure which material fits your property best, we can evaluate your roof's physical condition first and then discuss which options align with your project goals.
